Librogame.title: The Last Sacrifice
Librogame.author: Andrei Simion
Librogame.Blurb:
A metal ship rams the frozen shore and leaves you at the foot of the storm. Somewhere inside the white something is calling you, and you have wanted to answer it since the day you read that the king of the imperium was dead.
Three sacrifices stand between you and the centre of the storm. The second one costs you a hand, and the book remembers whether you paid it: what you can still do with your arms, later, in the dark, depends on that night in the cathedral.
Librogame.ContentWarnings: Mutilation, body horror, wounds described in detail, and the death of the character.

Changes.Change: Rewritten for this engine: the thirty-nine numbered entries, and where each of them leads, are the original's
Where the original asks you to roll a D6, the app rolls for you, with the odds the original gives
"If you chose to sacrifice your hand" is no longer a question asked of the reader: the book remembers that night and offers only the action you can actually take
The choices are written as actions instead of "If you choose to..., go to 20"
The scenes have no titles, as in the original: a heading above a scene would say what is about to happen
The original has no character sheet; this engine asks for one, so the book declares a single quality that nothing in it reads
Dialogue is marked with an em dash, where the original used a hyphen
Cover illustration not included: the original does not state its source
Added sounds and background music, delivered together with the book

Page.Text:
The metal ship rammed into the frozen shore. Outside the large window of the bridge, the storm roared. Ice crystals slammed against the ship's hull, their noise echoing through the rusty old pipes. The captain was an old fellow. He lay back in his seat, pipe in hand, looking into the dense fog of ice that swallowed his ship. In an old, ragged voice he said as if talking to himself.
— Seen 'em winds reach hundreds o'knots 'round these parts... air so bitter it’ll freeze a man in minutes...
You turned around and saw him looking at you with the corner of his eye.
— No shame in turnin' back now lad, better live a coward than die a fool. The sea’s got no mercy. She’ll tear the flesh clean off a man and leave yer frozen bones with the rest.

Choice.text: Ignore him and keep your eyes on the ice
Answer him and say why you came

Page.Text:
You were in your bed, in a small, dark apartment, typical for a place as crowded as the capital of the empire. Outside the wide windows of the 365th floor, the ever-stretching buildings of Vel Drathen cast dark shadows in the moonlight. A feeling of loneliness leaked in through the cracks in the walls, accompanied by a deep silence.
A creak broke your train of thought. You turned towards the door. A pair of pale eyes floated in the dark, unblinking. The creature straightened and stood up, filling the doorframe. It twisted its head, meeting your gaze.

Choice.text: Get up and go towards it
Stay where you are and watch it

Page.Text: The creature crashed into you, slamming you to the floor. Its full weight crushed your chest as claws sank deep into your flesh. Through its cracked ribs you could see its heart, throbbing with rage.

Choice.text: Reach into its ribs with the metal hand
Force the gun between its ribs

Page.Text:
You scared his gaze away with a disappointing look.
— I did not come this far to turn back at the first sign of trouble.
In the shadows of the room, Nevelir Valcor grinned, satisfied by your confidence. The captain turned back towards the storm and said quietly:
— Ain’t many left with your kind of spark, I’ll give ye that. But this place feeds on such ambitions. You take care out there lad.

Choice.text: Take the door out onto the ice

Page.Text: The machine screeched. You drove your metal hand through the creature's rib cage. Bone cracked. You wrenched free the creature’s heart. Blood spewed from its chest as it screamed in pain. Its corpse collapsed, crushing you beneath it. You shoved it aside and rose, trembling. In your hand, the heart, still beating, radiated a strange, comforting warmth.

Choice.text: Put the heart in your coat and walk on

Page.Text: The creature crashed into you, hurling you backward through the glass. Your head dangled over the building’s edge as it pinned you down, its claws carving into your flesh. Through its cracked ribs you could see its heart, throbbing with rage.

Choice.text: Drive the metal hand into its chest
Push the barrel against its heart

Page.Text:
You hesitated. Nevelir sensed your unease and disappointment clouded his face. He let the blade fall from his hand. Its metallic ring echoed through the cathedral as it struck the stone floor.
Ice crystals slammed against you, slicing your skin. The cold started to eat away at you. Your fingers trembled. You felt your body giving out, sinking into the snow. From the white void, something called to you. And you were closer than ever. Just a bit more. Just a bit closer. You rose and kept dragging yourself onward, step by step.

Choice.text: Drag yourself on through the snow

Page.Text: You dived aside as its claws raked the floor, splintering wood. It growled, baring its teeth, and turned for another leap. You steadied your gun.

Choice.text: Fire your gun into its skull
Hold your fire and let it come

Page.Text: You drove your boot into its skull. The creature reeled, its claws scraping at the metal frame. With a final scream, it reached for you, as it slipped, falling into the darkness of the night. Rain poured in through the shattered window. Shards of glass glittered across the floor like a field of knives.

Choice.text: Let the metal hand carry you on
Get up with what strength is left

Page.Text: The machine screeched. You drove your metal hand through the creature's rib cage. Bone cracked. You wrenched free the creature’s heart. Blood spewed from its chest as it screamed in pain. Its corpse collapsed, crushing you beneath it. You shoved it aside and rose, trembling. In your hand, the heart, still beating, radiated a strange, comforting warmth.

Choice.text: Close your hand around the heart

Page.Text:
The creature lunged. Its jaws wide open as its scream cut through the air.
[A six-sided die decides: four or higher and you get clear.]

Choice.text: Twist out of its path

Page.Text:
The First Sacrifice
You first saw it in a newspaper. The king of the imperium was dead. "Eaten by the storm" they called it. Without needing words, the idea had already taken root. Ignored at first, it lingered. Like a whisper, it spread through the corners of your mind until, one night, it could no longer be ignored.

Choice.text: Let the idea have its way

Page.Text: The storm had now reached its peak. From the pocket of your coat you pulled out the heart. You held it in your hand, still pounding, radiating a pleasant warmth. A dim flicker against the snow's frozen breath. You pushed forward, ice scoured your skin. The wind screamed. You buried your feet in the snow and dragged yourself onward, leaning against it, one heavy step at a time.

Choice.text: Lean into the wind and keep walking

Page.Text:
You sat like that for a moment, looking at each other in silence. Then, without a sound, the creature turned around and disappeared into the darkness of the other room.
It's getting bolder, you thought. It has never come this close before. Something had changed.

Choice.text: Go back to the drawings on the desk

Page.Text:
The storm had now reached its peak. Your eyes, burning with arrogant ambition, cut through the endless void. In the clouds above, the wind shrieked in anger. A sharp, sudden sound filled the air as pain flooded your body.
You fell in the snow. A tiny speck of red in the never-ending sea of white. As your vision darkened, you noticed a white flower, gently swaying in the wind. A faint smile touched your lips. The storm roared unconquered, its eternal winds sweeping across your frozen corpse.
You tried to kick the creature off. Its claws hooked into your leg. As it roared in desperation, it slipped off the ledge, dragging you with it into the endless dark.

Choice.text: Grab the ledge with the metal hand
Grab for the ledge with both hands

Page.Text: You took one last look at the ship's bridge before reaching for the heavy metal door. The moment it opened, a blast of freezing wind hit you, dragging snow and dust through the room. You stepped outside, disappearing into the white void and slamming the door shut behind you with a loud bang.

Choice.text: Walk on into the white

Page.Text: The storm had now reached its peak. Ice shards wiped through the air, slicing your skin. The cold started to eat away at you. Your fingers trembled. You felt your body giving out, sinking into the snow. The metal hand screeched, pushing you forward. Just a little further.

Choice.text: Keep dragging yourself forward

Page.Text:
You twisted aside. Pain seared your shoulder as its claw grazed you. Glass exploded behind you. A rush of cold, wet air flooded the room as rain lashed through the shattered window wall. The creature clung to the frame, claws screeching against metal.
You moved closer, trying to shove it off. Beyond the edge, the city stretched into a dark fog.
[A six-sided die decides: five or higher and your boot lands first.]

Choice.text: Kick it off the window frame

Page.Text:
You scared his gaze away with a disappointing look.
In the shadows of the room, Nevelir Valcor waited, watching. The captain turned back towards the storm and said quietly:
— Ain’t many left with your kind of spark, I’ll give ye that. But this place feeds on such ambitions. You take care out there lad.

Choice.text: Reach for the metal door

Page.Text:
The cathedral rose high above the capital, its stone arches stretching into shadow. Candles flickered, their flames bending in the heavy, waiting air that smelled faintly of smoke and metal.
At the center, on a stone altar, the idea was now complete. Nevelir stood behind it, visibly excited, a quality he rarely showed. Moving his hands in restless gestures, he said:
— How far we've come... When we started it was nothing but abstract lines. Now, it stands complete. We made it real! We made it perfect!
It was beautiful. The way the polished, curved metal folded over the joints, the way the tiny inner gears moved the delicate fingers, the way the muscles contracted, moving it with incredible precision. It was graceful. A perfect metal hand.
You gently placed your palm on it. The metal fibers stirred beneath your soft touch. It felt alive. Each tick of its gears felt like a warm heartbeat. Pressurized tubes and cables moved like veins beneath a metal skin. Filaments wrapped around strong steel bones like muscles. Its murmurs called out to you.
Nevelir's voice drowned them out:
— But an idea alone is not enough. Nothing is ever accomplished without sacrifice. You must prove you are ready to take the next step.
From beside the altar, he drew a long blade. Its edge caught the dim light as he held it out to you.
— A machine is nothing without its master. It needs a soul. Answer its call, and transcend your weak, human nature!

Choice.text: Take the blade from his hand
Refuse and let the blade fall

Page.Text: You jammed the gun between its ribs, pressing the barrel against its pulsing heart and pulled the trigger. Blood spewed from the creature's chest as it screamed in pain. Its corpse collapsed, crushing you beneath it. You shoved it aside and rose, trembling, standing over the twitching corpse.

Choice.text: Leave the corpse and go on

Page.Text:
You rose and stepped towards it. It retreated, maintaining its distance. You stared at each other in silence. Then, without a sound, the creature turned around and disappeared into the darkness of the other room.
It's getting bolder, you thought. It has never come this close before. Something had changed.

Choice.text: Go back to the desk and the papers

Page.Text:
Three more shots split the night. The creature shrieked, part of its skull fracturing. But it wasn’t enough. With a snarl, it sprang forward, jaws gaping.
[A six-sided die decides: four or higher and you twist out of its path.]

Choice.text: Twist aside as it comes

Page.Text:
You caught the ledge, the metal hand screeched under the strain, but held. The creature slammed into the wall below, its claws scrabbling upward. Its weight tore open your leg before it finally lost its grip and fell, screaming into the fog.
You hung there, trembling, then pulled yourself up.

Choice.text: Pull yourself up and go on

Page.Text: You jammed the gun between its ribs, pressing the barrel against its pulsing heart and pulled the trigger. Nothing. The chamber was empty. The creature opened its jaws wide, its throat glowed from within, heat searing through the air as fire built in its chest.

Choice.text: Watch the fire build in its chest

Page.Text:
You twisted aside. Pain seared your shoulder as its claw grazed you. Glass exploded behind you. A rush of cold, wet air flooded the room as rain lashed through the shattered window wall. The creature clung to the frame, claws screeching against metal.
You raised the gun, steadied your aim, and fired. The shot punched through its skull. It let out a distorted scream before slipping from the ledge and vanishing into the darkness below.

Choice.text: Let the metal hand carry you forward
Get up and walk on into the snow

Page.Text:
The Second Sacrifice
The idea had now taken shape. It stood before you on the paper. Its intricate gears formed a beautiful, elegant design, far beyond the technology of its time. It almost felt alive. When you closed your eyes, you could hear the faint tinkering of machinery. Whispers tempting you, waiting to be born, to be complete.
That's when you first met him. A shadow fell across your desk. A heavy hand rested on your shoulder. Nevelir's voice was soft but determined, trembling with reverence:
— It is beautiful, he muttered. Such an elegant masterpiece...
His fingers brushed the page, tracing the lines as though he could feel the curvature of the machine. He closed his eyes, took a deep breath, and a twisted grin appeared on his face:
— Ahh... can you smell it? Can you hear the sound of frozen metal? Yes... greatness awaits us...

Choice.text: Follow him to the cathedral

Page.Text: You jammed the gun between its ribs, pressing the barrel against its pulsing heart and pulled the trigger. Blood spewed from the creature's chest as it screamed in pain. Its corpse collapsed, crushing you beneath it. You shoved it aside and rose, trembling, standing over the twitching corpse.

Choice.text: Step over the corpse and go on

Page.Text:
The Third Sacrifice
You woke up again. The silence of the dark apartment pressed in like a heavy mist. Outside, rain battered the wide glass wall. Thoughts clawed through your mind, keeping you up. A creak silenced them. In the corner of the dimly lit room, a shadow crouched over scattered papers, whispering to itself. As if sensing your gaze, it turned towards you. Its pale eyes locked onto you, piercing your soul. It was Nevelir. He rose, blueprints slipping from his hands, fluttering to the floor like dead leaves.
— It isn't enough... he muttered, his voice barely a breath but filled with grim resolve. I must have more!
Veins bulged and writhed beneath his skin. Bone forced its way through his fingertips, hardening into claws. Dead vines, bristling with thorns, tore through him. A high, guttural rumble rose from his throat as his flesh withered to ash, peeling away to reveal the bone beneath. The creature roared, exposing teeth that glinted like blades in the moonlight. Its now hollow eyes stared at you.
You moved instinctively, rolling from the bed and seizing the revolver from the nightstand. Three shots thundered in the dark. The creature staggered, but did not fall. It roared. A deep, hollow sound. It lunged at you.
[A six-sided die decides where this goes: only a one, and it is already on top of you.]

Choice.text: Throw yourself off the bed

Page.Text:
Then, without warning, the sound died. The wind fell silent and the snow stopped falling. You stumbled a few more steps into the calm opening before you. The clouds above turned slowly, grinding like gears in a giant machine. You heard the storm's howl, now a distant faint rumble, hidden behind the tall grey frontier of the storm. A thin layer of snow covered the ground, undisturbed. You took a deep breath. The smell of frozen, clean air filled your lungs.
In the middle of the clearing was a simple, stone throne. Nevelir stood behind it, his hand resting on its back. He looked around in wonder, admiring the stillness of the storm's center.
— We made it, he said. We finally reached it... Come, embrace your destiny.
You took a step forward and your leg hit something in the snow. All around, scattered on the ground, white bones pierced through the thin snow. Hands, long dead, lay still, reaching for the throne.

Choice.text: Sit down on the stone throne
Turn your back on the throne

Page.Text: The machine screeched. You drove your metal hand through the creature's rib cage. Bone cracked. You wrenched free the creature’s heart. Blood spewed from its chest as it screamed in pain. Its corpse collapsed, crushing you beneath it. You shoved it aside and rose, trembling. In your hand, the heart, still beating, radiated a strange, comforting warmth.

Choice.text: Take the heart and go on

Page.Text:
You took one last look at the clearing, then turned away.
From behind you, Nevelir shouted:
— You're going to give it all up?! Now?! After everything?! You are nothing but a fool!
You stepped back into the storm, and the deafening roar swallowed his words.
Your wrinkled fingers brushed the old page. The blueprints, covered in dust, lay forgotten. Looking back, perhaps it had been nothing more than a pointless dream, fueled by hollow ambition. You turned off the light. Darkness swallowed the tiny room.

Full of resolve, you took the blade from his hand. The same twisted grin crept across his face, half-hidden in shadow.
Ice crystals slammed against you. You shielded your face with your arm. The metal shuddered, scratched by the snow. Buried deep in your elbow joint, the energy core powered metal fibers, turning gears, and sparking circuits that kept your body moving forward through the snow. Pushed to its limits, the contraption hissed, heating the air and melting the ice clinging to your clothes. You glared into the white void, something called to you. And you were closer than ever.

Choice.text: Walk on into the white void

Page.Text: The storm had now reached its peak. Ice raged around you and your fingers turned purple from frostbite. Your legs gave out, and you fell into the snow. In front of you, a single, white flower swayed in the wind, just out of reach. You crawled towards it, hand stretched, trembling through the snow. With your last breath, you pushed forward. Your hand fell still, inches from the stem. A faint smile touched your lips. The storm roared unconquered, its eternal winds sweeping across your frozen corpse.

The creature crashed into you, hurling you backward through the glass. Your head dangled over the building’s edge as it pinned you down, its claws carving into your flesh. Through its cracked ribs you could see its heart, throbbing with rage.

Choice.text: Put the metal hand through its ribs
Jam the gun against its heart

Page.Text: For a heartbeat, you felt weightless. The creature screamed behind you. Far above, the stars drifted indifferent, further than ever before. One by one, they vanished behind the never-ending buildings as the darkness swallowed you whole.

The white storm raged around you. In the dense ice fog that blocked your sight, something was calling out to you. You walked on, determined, pushing against the frozen winds. In the distance, a faint shadow formed. As you drew nearer you could make out the figure of a king. His hands opened wide in madness, his rasp voice loud as thunder as he cried into the void:
— O mighty storm! Hear thy master’s call! I stand before thee to claim what is mine! I am the lord of all beneath the heavens! The devourer of kingdoms! My hand spans the ends of the earth !... I command thee, kneel!
The storm's roar drowned out his voice. Winds rose faster and faster, ice crystals slicing through the air like tiny bullets. A gust of wind, sharp as a frozen blade, screamed past you from the clouds above. A piercing noise echoed in your skull and the snow in front of you was painted red. The former king was no more. His body cleaved in half, lying still on the frozen earth.
As you got closer, a faint light appeared in the storm. Not far from where he had fallen, a delicate white flower was growing, untouched by the wind's violence. Its elegant beauty was unlike anything you had ever seen. You reached out, mesmerized. But before your fingers could touch the stem, you opened your eyes.

Choice.text: Open your eyes on the dark

Page.Text:
You gently placed your fingers on the armrest, feeling the cold stone. Then, with a firm grip, you slowly sat down. In an instant, the storm stopped. The last shreds of snow fell to the ground as the sky cleared. An open icy field stretched as far as the eyes could see. In the distance, waves crashed into the frozen shore and a mountain range pierced the night sky. A gentle wind scattered ice crystals across the white dunes, shining in the moonlight like grains of white sand.
For the first time in a long while, you smiled. A feeling of greatness enveloped you, giving you a sense of satisfaction deeper than anything you had felt before. You were the first. Nature bent to your will. The storm was no more. An uncontrollable feeling of laughter took hold of you. It had all been worth it.
You looked at the frozen desert around you.
— Why come all the way out here anyway? What is so special about this place?
Nevelir stood next to you, his gaze lost somewhere on the horizon.
— Nothing. Not anymore.
You smiled at the thought.
A sharp pain bloomed. Veins writhed and pulsed as vines pierced through your skin, sprouting new life. Your hands clenched the cold throne. Slowly, your body turned to ash, leaving only metal and bone. You lifted your head to the night sky and gazed in awe at the distant stars. They seemed to stare back, as if noticing you for the first time. Your jaw split open. From within, vines unfurled, revealing a single, white bulb. It blossomed into a delicate flower, its petals trembling with a quiet grace.
Around it, the white desert stood silent.
Metal and bone, forever frozen in the cold winds of time.
